After calling play() (as a player who previously wagered) and then AdjustDifficulty by the owner, the contract's currentDifficulty() must be strictly positive.
Calling play() (as a real player who wagered) then AdjustDifficulty(amount) by the owner preserves that currentDifficulty() is equal to the last emitted DifficultyChanged() value.

After calling play() (which in P may set difficulty via AdjustDifficulty later), calling AdjustDifficulty(amount) by the owner makes currentDifficulty() equal to the provided amount in the original contract but not in the mutant — so require that currentDifficulty() equals amount after the call.

For any uint256 newDifficulty, calling AdjustDifficulty(newDifficulty) by the owner updates C.currentDifficulty() to equal the provided newDifficulty; the mutant fails because it emits the event but leaves difficulty unchanged for some inputs.

For any uint256 newDifficulty and when called by the owner, AdjustDifficulty(newDifficulty) updates the contract's difficulty to equal newDifficulty; the mutant emits the event but leaves difficulty unchanged, so for some fuzzed newDifficulty values the mutant's difficulty differs from the provided value while the reference always sets it.

For every uint256 newDifficulty and when AdjustDifficulty is called by the owner, the reference contract's public getter currentDifficulty() equals the newDifficulty after the call; the mutant emits an event but leaves difficulty unchanged so for some fuzzed newDifficulty values the getter does not equal the provided value.

For any owner who calls AdjustBetAmounts(x), the reference contract leaves difficulty unchanged except when AdjustDifficulty was previously called to change it; the mutant emits DifficultyChanged but never lets difficulty change when owner later calls AdjustBetAmounts(x) followed by AdjustDifficulty(y) (i.e., calling AdjustBetAmounts must not affect the ability to change difficulty afterwards — in the reference difficulty reflects the most recent AdjustDifficulty call, while the mutant can make difficulty stuck/unchanged), so there exists some sequence where reference reports new difficulty but mutant does not.

For every uint256 delta set by the owner via AdjustBetAmounts, calling AdjustDifficulty afterwards with any fuzzed newDifficulty results in the contract's currentDifficulty() equaling that newDifficulty in the reference; the mutant (which removed the assignment in AdjustDifficulty) will violate this for some fuzzed newDifficulty values because difficulty remains unchanged.
